name: AI agents and workflow automation
summary: Software agents carry out bounded sequences of work across applications, with people approving consequential actions.
useCase: A procurement agent checks a purchase request against policy, retrieves approved suppliers, drafts an order and routes exceptions to a buyer.
whyNow: Large-company deployment is expanding: McKinsey’s 2026 survey reports 40% scaling agents, versus 27% in 2025. However, the outcome depends on integration, permissions and reliable exception handling. Buying an agent license does not establish that autonomous work is useful or economical. The opportunity is strongest when the task has clear inputs, an observable result and a safe recovery path.

mainstream.scope: Routine production use of agents for selected, repeatable enterprise workflows, with human approval and monitoring.
mainstream.rationale: The survey shows movement beyond experimentation, while Gartner’s 2028 application forecast supports broad distribution. Widespread dependable execution should lag product availability. The window assumes identity controls, evaluations and operational ownership improve. Complex cross-company decisions may remain supervised well after 2035.

metric.name: Large organizations scaling AI agents
metric.scope: McKinsey respondents at organizations with annual revenue above US$1 billion.
metric.limitations: Survey estimates, not a census or verified production transaction count; respondent mix may change. This is the large-company subgroup, not all businesses. No defensible annual series for 2021–2024 is supplied.
metric.futureNote: The forward curve is an analyst maturity scenario. Gartner’s enterprise-application forecast uses a different denominator and is displayed separately.

outlookMetrics.name: Enterprise software applications containing agentic AI
outlookMetrics.note: Published June 2025; baseline below 1% in 2024. This measures applications, not organizations scaling agents.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No comparable agent-deployment measurement identified; earlier automation should not be relabeled as modern LLM agents.
No comparable measurement identified for enterprise agents; the maturity score is an analyst assessment.
No comparable global deployment count identified; evaluate bounded tool use separately from ordinary chatbots.
Gartner later estimated fewer than 1% of enterprise applications contained agentic AI.
27% of surveyed large organizations were scaling agents; Microsoft reported over 230,000 organizations using Copilot Studio.
Reported scaling reached 40% of large organizations; the survey still distinguishes scaling from enterprise-wide value.

tailwinds: Agents can be distributed through existing workflow and cloud software.
Better tool interfaces and evaluation systems make narrow tasks easier to automate.
bottlenecks: Error recovery, prompt injection and excessive permissions can make unattended execution costly.
Gartner forecasts more than 40% of agentic projects may be canceled by the end of 2027; a forecast, not an observed cancellation rate.
watchMetrics: Share of eligible transactions completed correctly without intervention; report exception and rollback rates.
Cost per verified completed task and renewal rates, rather than demonstrations or raw token consumption.
